content.title: About
content.content: Seafood salad is a cold dish made from a mixture of cooked or poached seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid, crab meat) combined with vegetables, herbs, and a light dressing based on mayonnaise, yogurt or olive oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Seafood salad is a staple in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.
There are many variations, including avocado, mango, rice or noodle additions.
Seafood is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are heart‑healthy.
The salad is often served as an appetizer at festive gatherings and seafood restaurants.
Lemon or lime juice is commonly added for a bright, tangy flavor.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Seafood provides EPA and DHA, fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The salad supplies all essential amino acids, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: It contains zinc, iron, iodine, vitamin B12 and vitamin D, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low calorie with light dressing
items.content: Using a yogurt‑based or olive‑oil dressing keeps the dish light yet satisfying.

items.title: Supports brain function
items.content: Omega‑3 and vitamin B12 contribute to improved cognition and mood.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or other shellfish.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Improperly handled seafood can harbor bacteria and toxins; ensure thorough cooking and proper storage.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared dressings and canned seafood often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Certain seafood (e.g., crab meat) contains cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as an appetizer or light main. Pair it with whole‑grain bread, crackers, or use it as a filling for wraps. For a lighter option, swap mayonnaise for a yogurt‑herb dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, store seafood and vegetables separately and combine just before serving.
